Type
class

Homebrew caster class from GM Binder. The Bastion is an innate sei-manipulator who can absorb and redirect magical energy. Uses the Cleric spell list with Charisma-based known spellcasting (not prepared). d6 hit die, no armor, and a unique Overload Pool mechanic that rewards absorbing enemy spells at physical cost.

Description

Few in the world have the ability and resolve to stand toe to toe with a master seimaster and live to tell the tale. The Bastion has an innate binding to the flow of sei, and has the ability to shape magic — even magic already shaped by other casters and creatures. The flow of sei molds them into charismatic leaders destined to do great things.

The Bastion specializes in stopping the misuse of magic: from the necromancer raising an army of dead to hags feeding on the life force of captured children, a Bastion uses their abilities to help those in need. Because of their charismatic nature, the raw power they can hold, and the ease at which they handle difficult individuals, Bastions are often found as leaders later in life.

There are few Bastions in the world. No one knows how a mortal becomes one, but each generation produces only a handful. The bond with the flow of sei can tear at mental capacity and even impact physical health.

Quick Reference

  • Hit Die: d6 (6 + Con at 1st; 1d6 + Con per level after)
  • Saves: Charisma, Constitution
  • Armor: None
  • Weapons: Simple weapons
  • Tools: None
  • Skills: Pick 3 from Arcana, Deception, History, Insight, Intimidation, Medicine, Perception, Religion
  • Spellcasting: Cleric spell list, Charisma-based, known spells (not prepared)
  • Subclass pick at: Level 3 (Bastion Order)
  • Subclass features at: 3, 5, 10, 18
  • Restriction: Cannot multiclass with other caster classes

Starting Equipment

  • (a) any simple weapon, staff, or warhammer
  • (a) a sling and 20 stones
  • (a) an adventurer's pack or (b) a priest's pack

Quick Build

Charisma is your primary stat — it drives AC, spellcasting, and most class features. Constitution provides HP to absorb more magical energy. Dexterity improves AC and reflexive capabilities.

Progression Table

Lvl PB Features Cantrips Spells Known 1st 2nd 3rd 4th 5th 6th 7th
1 +2 Spellcasting, Unarmored Defense 2 2 1 — — — — — —
2 +2 Spell Absorption 2 3 2 — — — — — —
3 +2 Bastion Order 2 4 2 1 — — — — —
4 +2 ASI 2 5 3 1 — — — — —
5 +3 Order Feature, Bolster Spell 3 6 3 2 — — — — —
6 +3 — 3 7 3 2 1 — — — —
7 +3 Magic Field 3 8 3 2 2 — — — —
8 +3 ASI 3 9 3 3 2 — — — —
9 +4 — 3 10 3 3 2 1 — — —
10 +4 Arcane Sight, Order Feature 3 11 3 3 3 1 — — —
11 +4 — 3 12 3 3 3 1 1 — —
12 +4 ASI 4 12 3 3 3 2 1 — —
13 +5 Absorbing Touch 4 13 3 3 3 3 1 — —
14 +5 Arcane Appetite 4 13 3 3 3 3 2 — —
15 +5 — 4 14 3 3 3 3 2 1 —
16 +5 ASI 4 14 3 3 3 3 2 1 —
17 +6 — 4 15 3 3 3 3 2 1 1
18 +6 Order Feature 4 15 3 3 3 3 2 1 1
19 +6 ASI 4 15 3 3 3 3 2 1 1
20 +6 Divine Mastery 4 15 3 3 3 3 2 1 1

Core Class Features (Summaries)

Paraphrased from the source. Consult the GM Binder document for full rules text.

  • Spellcasting (1): Uses the Cleric spell list with Charisma as the casting stat. Known spells (not prepared) — learn 2 at 1st level and more as shown in the table. Can swap one known spell per level-up. Ritual casting supported. Spellcasting focus: holy symbol, staff, or wand.
    • Spell save DC = 8 + PB + CHA mod
    • Spell attack = PB + CHA mod
  • Unarmored Defense (1): While wearing no armor, AC = 10 + DEX mod + CHA mod.
  • Spell Absorption (2): As a reaction when an enemy you can see within 60 ft casts a spell, you can absorb it. The absorbed spell's levels are distributed among your empty spell slots. You may make an Arcana check against the caster's DC to identify the spell first. Range increases to 120 ft at 12th level and 180 ft at 16th level.
    • Overload Pool: Spell levels that cannot fit into empty slots go into an overload pool. Using overload magic to cast costs 1d6 max HP per overload level used (not mitigable; restored on long rest).
    • Mass Discharge: At end of your turn, if overload is not empty, the raw magic discharges: 1d10 psychic per overload point to yourself, and every creature within 15 ft makes an INT save (DC 12 + overload points) for half.
  • Bastion Order (3): Choose a subclass: Order of the Sword, Order of the Shield, or Order of the Staff. Features at 3, 5, 10, 18.
  • Bolster Spell (5): You can use overload points to upcast a spell (up to your max spell level). Cannot use this to cast higher-level spells you don't have slots for — only to increase the casting level of a spell already being cast from a slot.
  • Magic Field (7): When you are the target of a magical effect or within a spell's area, make a CHA save (DC 14 + spell level). On failure, you automatically absorb the spell via Spell Absorption. This is not considered magical for advantage purposes.
  • Arcane Sight (10): You permanently see as if detect magic is cast. At 14th level, you gain truesight.
  • Absorbing Touch (13): As an action, absorb one spell effect on yourself or one willing creature you touch. Uses: CHA mod per long rest.
  • Arcane Appetite (14): You are resistant to magic and magical effects.
  • Divine Mastery (20): Cast one 8th-level and one 9th-level spell per long rest from a specific list:
    • 8th: Antimagic Field, Control Weather, Dominate Monster, Earthquake, Holy Aura, Mind Blank, Sunburst
    • 9th: Invulnerability, Mass Heal, Prismatic Wall, True Resurrection, Wish

Orders of the Bastion (Subclasses)

1. Order of the Sword — Offensive magic focus. Uses the flow of sei to empower spells and minimize overload cost when on the attack.

  • Divine Precision (3): Bonus action: +10 to a ranged spell attack roll (after seeing the roll, before result). Uses: CHA mod per long rest.
  • Managed Overload (5): Add CHA mod to damage on single-target spells cast from overload. Take half the max HP damage when using overload for ranged spell attacks.
  • Divine Leverage (10): Advantage on spell attacks made entirely from overload magic. Bolstered spells (slot + overload) do not benefit.
  • Divine Retribution (18): When casting a single-target spell, duplicate it to a second target using overload levels equal to the spell level. Uses: CHA mod per long rest.

2. Order of the Shield — Defensive and protection focus. Manipulates the flow of sei to ward allies and resist harmful effects.

  • Divine Ward (3): Bonus action: expend a spell slot to place a ward on a creature within 30 ft. Ward absorbs 1d6 damage per spell slot level.
  • Improved Divine Ward (5): Warded creatures have resistance to non-magical piercing, bludgeoning, and slashing. Bastion adds PB to WIS saves.
  • Divine Protection (10): Immune to disease, poison damage, and the poisoned condition.
  • Divine Guard (18): Resistant to magic and magical effects (except Mass Discharge).

3. Order of the Staff — Healing and support focus. Uses divine energy to keep allies at full capacity.

  • Divine Gifts (3): Grant an inspiration die to an ally within 60 ft. The creature adds it to one ability check, attack, or save (decide after d20 roll, before result). Alternatively, use it as a heal (add CHA mod). Die scales: d6 (3rd), d8 (7th), d10 (13th), d12 (17th). Uses: CHA mod per long rest.
  • Blessed Soul (5): When you cast a healing spell on another creature, you heal 2 + spell level HP. Take half the max HP damage when using overload to heal allies.
  • Evasion (10): DEX saves for half damage become no damage on success, half on failure.
  • Supreme Healing (18): Reroll any 1s and 2s on healing dice (must use the new roll).

frontmatter.name: Buddhist Monk
tools: one artisan tool or musical instrument (player choice)

description.value:
Type
class

Homebrew Monk variant from D&D Wiki. This is the class Sun Wukong is built on — not the SRD monk. Mechanical differences (d10 hit die, doubled ki pool, front-loaded level 6) matter for balance and should be noted in session prep.

See pcs/sun-wukong.md for the active character and npcs/elder-benkei.md for the order's elder.

Description

A discipline of armed and unarmed combat taught in the monasteries of Seizan and Hokori's mountain orders. Buddhist Monks of this path — the Tranquil Lotus among them — train the body as an instrument of ki and follow one of twelve Ways. Where an SRD monk is a lightly armored martial artist, the Buddhist Monk leans harder into ki expenditure, tool mastery, and a broader weapon repertoire (simple and martial proficiency).

Quick Reference

  • Hit Die: d10 (10 + Con at 1st; 1d10 + Con per level after)
  • Saves: Dexterity, Wisdom
  • Armor: Light only
  • Weapons: Simple and martial
  • Tools: One artisan's tool or musical instrument (player choice)
  • Skills: Pick 3 from Acrobatics, Athletics, History, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Religion, Stealth
  • Subclass pick at: Level 3 (Way of the Monk)
  • Subclass features at: 3, 6, 11, 17

Starting Equipment

  • (a) one martial weapon of your choice or (b) two simple weapons of your choice
  • (a) an explorer's pack or (b) a dungeoneer's pack
  • Alternative starting wealth: 2d4 × 10 gp

Progression Table

Paraphrased from the source; see wiki for full text. Ki pool and Martial Arts die scaling are the most distinctive numbers in this variant.

Lvl PB Martial Arts Ki Points Unarm. Move Key Features Gained
1 +2 1d6 — +10 ft Unarmored Mastery, Martial Arts
2 +2 1d6 4 + Wis +10 ft Ki, Body Improvements
3 +2 1d6 6 + Wis +10 ft Way of the Monk, Ki Enhancement, Deflect Projectiles
4 +2 1d6 8 + Wis +10 ft ASI, Slow Fall, Unlocked Ki
5 +3 1d8 10 + Wis +15 ft Extra Attack, Stunning Strike
6 +3 1d8 12 + Wis +15 ft Ki-Empowered Strikes, Monk Training, Way feature, ASI
7 +3 1d8 14 + Wis +15 ft Resistant, Stillness of Mind
8 +3 1d8 16 + Wis +15 ft ASI, Ki-Enhanced Critical
9 +4 1d10 18 + Wis +20 ft Ki Recovery
10 +4 1d10 20 + Wis +20 ft Limit Break, Purity of Body, Unlocked Ki (2)
11 +4 1d10 22 + Wis +20 ft Advanced Energy Usage, Extra Attack (2), Way feature
12 +4 1d10 24 + Wis +20 ft ASI, Advanced Monk Training
13 +5 1d12 26 + Wis +25 ft Tongue of the Sun and Moon
14 +5 1d12 28 + Wis +25 ft Diamond Soul, Limit Break (2)
15 +5 2d6 30 + Wis +25 ft Timeless Body
16 +5 2d6 32 + Wis +25 ft ASI, Ultimate Monk Training
17 +6 2d8 34 + Wis +30 ft Way feature
18 +6 2d8 36 + Wis +30 ft Empty Body, Limit Break (3)
19 +6 2d8 38 + Wis +30 ft ASI
20 +6 2d8 40 + Wis +30 ft Enlightenment

Core Class Features (Summaries)

Paraphrased. Consult the source wiki for full rules text and exact costs.

  • Unarmored Mastery (1): While unarmored and without a shield, AC = 10 + Dex + Wis; gain bonus speed and can run along walls or across water while ki is active. Gains a limited flight option at 9 while holding at least 1 ki.
  • Martial Arts (1): Use Dex for unarmed and monk-weapon attacks; substitute the Martial Arts die for normal damage; get a bonus-action unarmed strike whenever you Attack with an unarmed strike or monk weapon.
  • Ki (2): Pool of ki points recovered on a short rest after 30 minutes of meditation. Base uses: Flurry of Blows (1 ki, two bonus-action strikes), Patient Defense (1 ki, Dodge as bonus action), Step of the Wind (1 ki, Dash/Disengage as bonus action, doubled jump, no OA). Ki save DC = 8 + PB + Wis.
  • Body Improvements (2): Proficiency in Perception and Insight (doubled if already proficient).
  • Way of the Monk (3): Pick a subclass; features at 3, 6, 11, 17.
  • Ki Enhancement (3): Pick one of Empowered Strike, Energy Armor, or Weapon Enhancement — each burns ki for different offensive/defensive riders.
  • Deflect Projectiles (3): Reaction reduces ranged damage by Martial Arts die + Dex + monk level; reducing to 0 lets you throw the projectile back for 1 ki. Extra dedicated reactions unlock at 8 and 13.
  • Slow Fall (4): Reaction reduces falling damage by 5 × monk level.
  • Unlocked Ki (4, 10): Adds Abundant Step, Focused Aim, Ki Sphere at 4; Iron Fist, Karmic Strike, Weakening Touch, and Ki Surge at 10.
  • Extra Attack (5, 11): Two attacks at 5, three at 11.
  • Stunning Strike (5): 1 ki on a melee hit forces a Con save or stun until end of your next turn. Later options let you paralyze or blind instead.
  • Ki-Empowered Strikes (6): Unarmed strikes (or monk weapons, your pick) count as magical and add a Wisdom-scaled damage die. Both options become magical at 11.
  • Monk Training / Advanced / Ultimate (6, 12, 16): Bonus feats chosen from curated Body, Martial Arts, Ki, Ki Manipulation, and Healing feat lists, with one non-level prerequisite waived.
  • Resistant (7): Pick a high ability (16+); successful saves of that ability for half damage now take no damage, failures take half. A second option unlocks at 17.
  • Stillness of Mind (7): Action to remove charmed or frightened from yourself.
  • Ki-Enhanced Critical (8): While you have at least 1 ki, crit range expands to 19–20; at 16, 18–20.
  • Ki Recovery (9): Regain 1 ki at the start of each of your combat turns.
  • Limit Break (10, 14, 18): +2 to Str or Dex (pick), Con, and Wis, raising the cap — to 22 at 10, 24 at 14, 26 at 18.
  • Purity of Body (10): Immune to disease and poison.
  • Advanced Energy Usage (11): Pick two "ki energy use" options — imbuing objects into improvised weapons, rendering them volatile, etc. Ki costs scale with object size.
  • Tongue of the Sun and Moon (13): Understand and be understood in any spoken language.
  • Diamond Soul (14): Proficient in all saves; spend 1 ki to reroll a failed save.
  • Timeless Body (15): No aging, no need for food or water, spend ki to extend breath-holding.
  • Empty Body (18): 4 ki for 1-minute invisibility with resistance to all damage except force; 6 ki to cast astral projection on yourself.
  • Enlightenment (20): +4 to Str or Dex, Con, and Wis. Once per turn activate a 1-ki feature free. Bonus action to regain (2 × Wis mod) ki, uses = ½ PB. Spend 1 ki to manifest a Third Eye — 20 ft truesight and immunity to surprise for 1 min.

Ways of the Monk (Subclasses)

Twelve subclasses are available, each granting features at 3, 6, 11, and 17. Short original summaries:

  1. Ki Manipulator — scholar-monk path specializing in ki efficiency, ally healing, and high-level elemental "Deva" transformations.
  2. Sun Soul — channels ki as searing radiant light and solar bolts.
  3. Astral Self — manifests a spectral inner self (arms, face, body) that fights with force damage.
  4. Living Weapon — pure martial body-hardening path focused on stacked unarmed strikes and an awakened combat state.
  5. Drunken Master — unpredictable brawler who drinks for buffs, redirects attacks, and eventually breathes fire.
  6. Kensei — treats weapons as monk weapons, adds medium armor training, and layers combat techniques onto flurries and parries.
  7. Long Death — studies mortality, draining vitality as temp HP and inflicting fear and necrotic damage.
  8. Mercy — wandering healer-monks whose hands can soothe or wound, combining necrotic strikes with potent ki-powered healing pools.
  9. Shadow — ninja-flavored shadow-benders who hide in dim light and move unseen.
  10. Open Hand — classic pressure-point path controlling the battlefield via knockdown, shove, and reaction suppression through Flurry of Blows.
  11. Four Elements — elemental spellcaster-monks converting ki into fire, water, earth, or air discipline effects.
  12. Cobalt Soul — investigator-monks who "analyze" enemies to learn resistances and vulnerabilities, then exploit that intel with extra reactions.

description.value:
Akabana 紅花 (Crimson Bloom)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 7 days fresh; indefinitely dried
Tools: Herbalism kit; heat-resistant gloves
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A heat-loving flower found growing in volcanic ash near active vents in Hi province. The petals are a vivid crimson that deepens to black at the edges. When dried and crumbled into food, they produce a slow, building warmth that starts in the chest and spreads to the extremities. Hi province healers use them to treat exposure and hypothermia.

DM Notes

A genuine cold-weather remedy — the warmth is mechanical, not flavour. Hi province healers carry dried petals on any winter expedition into Sora or Kōri-no-Mori.

items.name: Arashi-suji 嵐筋 (Storm-Sinew)

description.value:
Arashi-suji 嵐筋 (Storm-Sinew)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Rare
Source: One-Time (Yama-no-Ōkami harvest)
Preservation: 2 days fresh; 14 days dried
Tools: Cook's utensils (slow-braise preparation)
Restrictions: One-time only

Long tendons drawn from the legs and spine. Under the right light they carry a faint static shimmer — a residue of the creature's connection to the high mountain storms. Slow-braised into broth they impart a tension to the muscles of those who drink it, a wound-tight readiness that lingers into the following day. Suitable for a Refined dish.

DM Notes

The "readiness" is a mechanical buff granted by a Refined dish prepared with Arashi-suji — bonus to initiative or first-action advantage for the following day depending on cook's preparation. Confirm buff wording against the recipe system when Phase 4 lands.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Storm-Sinew
unidentified.description: Long pale tendons, translucent and slightly elastic, with a faint prickling that brushes against the skin when handled in dim light.

items.name: Arashi-take 嵐茸 (Storm Cap) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Arashi-take 嵐茸 (Storm Cap)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Withers within a day of picking; must be consumed or preserved immediately; dried fragments retain a faint tingle
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); storm tracking
Restrictions: Only appears for 12–24 hours after a severe storm
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Found only on exposed surfaces after severe storms — typically on shattered tree trunks or freshly exposed rock faces in Nami province. The caps appear within hours of a major storm and wither within a day. They are electric blue with branching white patterns on the cap that resemble lightning. The flavor is sharp, almost astringent, with a tingling quality on the tongue.

DM Notes

Opportunistic — only harvestable after storms. Nami coastal specialty.

unidentified.description: An electric-blue mushroom with bright white branching patterns across its cap, growing on a shattered tree trunk after a storm.

items.name: Ayu 鮎 (Sweetfish) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Ayu 鮎 (Sweetfish)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Common
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 1 day fresh; 7 days salted; indefinitely dried
Tools: Fishing tackle, cormorant (traditional), or bare hands
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Slender river fish prized for the distinctive cucumber-melon scent of their flesh in the height of summer. Grilled whole on a split-bamboo skewer over charcoal, salted simply, the belly fat melts and the skin crisps. The single most perfect expression of a summer river in Hokori.

DM Notes

The quintessential summer river fish. Tradition holds the very best ayu come from the upper Kinryūgawa in late Natsu. A master fisher can catch them bare-handed in shallow riffles; most use tackle or traditional cormorant fishing.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Sweetfish
unidentified.description: Slim silver-green fish, eight to ten inches long, with delicate iridescent scales and the faint melon scent that rises from them as they warm.

Category: Niku
Rarity: Common
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 1 day fresh; 7 days salted; indefinitely dried
Tools: Fishing tackle, cormorant (traditional), or bare hands
Grade: 特上 Tokujō (craft modifier: +2)

Slender river fish prized for the distinctive cucumber-melon scent of their flesh in the height of summer. Grilled whole on a split-bamboo skewer over charcoal, salted simply, the belly fat melts and the skin crisps. The single most perfect expression of a summer river in Hokori.

DM Notes

The quintessential summer river fish. Tradition holds the very best ayu come from the upper Kinryūgawa in late Natsu. A master fisher can catch them bare-handed in shallow riffles; most use tackle or traditional cormorant fishing.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Sweetfish
unidentified.description: Slim silver-green fish, eight to ten inches long, with delicate iridescent scales and the faint melon scent that rises from them as they warm.

items.name: Bo

description.value:
Description

A straight staff of hardwood roughly six feet in length, the bo is the most democratic weapon in Kagekuni — anyone can cut one from a tree. Monks of the Tranquil Lotus train with the bo for decades, turning a simple stick into a blur of strikes and deflections. Peasants carry them as walking staves on the road, and no checkpoint guard questions a traveler with a bo.

items.name: Chigiriki

description.value:
Description

A short staff or handle with a weighted iron ball or chain attached to one end, the chigiriki is an anti-armor weapon that wraps around shields and strikes over guards. Sohei warriors train with it to defeat armored opponents where blades would glance off. The swinging weight builds tremendous momentum, though the weapon demands skill to avoid striking oneself.

items.name: Chōrei Miso 長齢味噌 (Longevity Miso) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Chōrei Miso 長齢味噌 (Longevity Miso)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: Rare
Source: Traded (monastery gift)
Preservation: Indefinite
Tools: None
Restrictions: Rarely sold for coin; usually given in exchange for service
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A miso aged for over a century in cedar casks at specific Buddhist monasteries, passed from generation to generation of temple cooks who tend each cask as an inheritance. The colour is nearly black and the flavour is impossibly deep — a single spoonful transforms an entire pot of broth. The monks who tend the casks rarely sell chōrei miso for coin; it is more often given in exchange for service or as a gift to honoured guests. A small jar is a meaningful reward for a completed quest.

DM Notes

**Quest-reward tier.** Use for monks-and-temples plotlines.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Longevity Miso
unidentified.description: A small ceramic jar of nearly-black miso with a smell like deep earth and old cedar.

description.value:
Dashi-kake 出汁掛け (Dried Dashi — Seaweed & Fish Stock)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: Common
Source: Traded (processed)
Preservation: Almost indefinite in dry storage
Tools: None
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Small bricks or loose powders of concentrated stock base, combining dried kombu kelp with katsuobushi flakes or occasionally dried sardines. A pinch dissolved in hot water produces instant broth — the backbone of every road meal from mushroom soup to trail ramen. Lightweight, compact, and keeps almost indefinitely.

DM Notes

Instant broth. A single brick makes several portions.

items.name: Dokuro-take 髑髏茸 (Skull Cap) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Dokuro-take 髑髏茸 (Skull Cap)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Dries well; holds medicinal properties for years
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); stomach for its habitat
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A bone-white mushroom found growing on ancient remains — specifically on buried skeletal material in battlefields, old gravesites, and ruined settlements. The cap is smooth and rounded, unsettlingly skull-like. Despite its morbid habitat, the flavor is mild and pleasant. Herbalists in Kaze province use it as a base for medicines that ease pain and promote rest.

DM Notes

**Narrative hook:** Disturbing an old burial has consequences — particularly in haunted biomes. Use sparingly in sacred ground.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Skull Cap
unidentified.description: A smooth, bone-white, skull-round mushroom pushing up from loose soil over what may once have been a grave.

Eringi エリンギ (King Trumpet)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged (Saishū)

The "meat" mushroom; prized in rural stews.

items.name: Fuetsu

description.value:
Description

A massive double-bitted or broad-headed war axe requiring two hands and considerable strength to wield, the fuetsu is favored by Zirak berserkers and the northern mountain clans. The name carries ceremonial weight — fuetsu were once used in ritual executions, and the weapon retains an air of grim authority. Each swing carries enough force to cleave through shield and arm together.

items.name: Fuki 蕗 (Butterbur) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Fuki 蕗 (Butterbur)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 3 days fresh; indefinitely pickled
Tools: Herbalism kit; cook's utensils for blanching
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A tall, broad-leafed plant with thick celery-like stalks that push up through the snow in early spring. The stalks are peeled, blanched, and simmered to remove a lingering bitterness — the reward is a clean fresh flavour that announces the end of winter. A beloved sign of the turning year in every mountain village.

DM Notes

Mountain villages hold small informal celebrations when the first fuki of the year is harvested. A reliable early-spring food source.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Butterbur
unidentified.description: Thick pale-green fleshy stalks, each as long as a forearm, topped with broad flat leaves.

description.value:
Description

A slender bamboo tube roughly three feet long, the fukiya launches tiny darts with a sharp breath. Nearly silent and easily disguised as a flute or walking stick, it is the preferred weapon for delivering poison at range without alerting guards. Hunters use them for small game; agents of the Order of the Black Lily use them for targets that must not know they are being attacked until the poison takes hold.

description.value:
Gin-en 銀塩 (Silver Salt)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Indefinite
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); knowledge of Ginryū's historical sites
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Pale, almost transparent crystal deposits found in caverns near the Silver Dragon's associated sites. The crystals are cold to the touch regardless of ambient temperature and dissolve with a clean, bright flavor followed by a cooling sensation that lingers. Used in dishes meant to counteract heat or fever, or simply as a finishing seasoning of extraordinary refinement.

DM Notes

Ginryū connection. Used in heat-cooling medicinal dishes.

items.name: Ginrei-sō 銀嶺草 (Silver Spirit Herb) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Ginrei-sō 銀嶺草 (Silver Spirit Herb)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 7 days fresh; indefinitely dried
Tools: Herbalism kit; cook's utensils for proper preparation
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A frost-white herb that grows at extreme altitude on the Hoshimori Plateau, where it clings to rock faces in thin soil that freezes solid every night. The leaves are tough and fibrous — useless raw — but when simmered they release a clean, piercingly bright flavour that clears the sinuses and sharpens the mind. Sora's observatory seimasters brew it as a study aid.

DM Notes

Traditional tea of the Hoshimori seimaster community. Three cups is said to keep a man alert through a full night of astronomical observation.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Silver Spirit Herb
unidentified.description: Frost-pale leaves that feel cold even in the hand, fibrous and tough.

Road-margin staple. Common gift from rural NPCs.

items.name: Hankyu

description.value:
Description

A short asymmetric bow, smaller than its battlefield cousin the yumi, the hankyu is favored by scouts, mounted skirmishers, and ronin who need a compact ranged weapon for travel. Its reduced draw weight limits range and penetration, but its portability makes it invaluable for those who cannot carry a full-sized bow. Many are lacquered and wrapped in rattan for weather resistance.

items.name: Haratake 原茸 (Meadow Cap) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Haratake 原茸 (Meadow Cap)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Fresh 2 days; dries adequately
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); a failure to identify correctly runs real risk of deadly lookalike
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Round, white-capped mushrooms found in open grasslands and grazed meadows, particularly where horses or cattle have passed. They push up in rings overnight after rain. The flavour is mild and slightly sweet — the most forgiving mushroom for new foragers, but also the easiest to mistake for dangerous lookalikes. Experienced gatherers teach children the telltale pink-to-brown gill colour.

DM Notes

**Risk flag:** easily mistaken for a deadly lookalike. Unproficient foragers should roll with disadvantage on identification; a failed identification at low grade may merit a poisoning check. --- **上 Jō — Uncommon**

unidentified.name: Unidentified Meadow Cap
unidentified.description: Round white-capped mushrooms pushing up through grazed meadow grass, gills underneath showing a faint pink colour.

description.value:
Hato 鳩 (Pigeon)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Common
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 2 days fresh; 10 days hung
Tools: Sling, bow, or net; cook's utensils for dressing
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Dark-meated city and cliff pigeons. The flesh is rich and earthy, with the kind of bold flavour that stands up to a hot grill and a sharp vinegar dressing. A cheap, nearly-free protein for travellers who know how to drop a bird from a temple eave with a sling.

DM Notes

Abundant around ruins and temple complexes — Haikyo is a particularly productive hunting ground. A party camping in a temple ruin can easily supplement rations with a pigeon or two per evening. --- **Uncommon**

unidentified.name: Unidentified Pigeon
unidentified.description: Plucked grey-rose birds the size of a man's clenched fist, rose-dark meat showing through at the wing joints.

description.value:
Hinotake 火茸 (Fire Stalk)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Dries stable; retains mild spice
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); **thick gloves required — raw caps cause chemical burns**
Restrictions: Hi province volcanic zones; fire-resistance preferred for ideal conditions
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Bright orange mushrooms that grow near volcanic vents in Hi province. The flesh is dry and slightly spicy. They thrive in temperatures that would kill any other fungus, drawing nutrients from volcanic mineral deposits. Must be handled carefully — the raw caps cause mild chemical burns on bare skin.

DM Notes

**Handling hazard:** 1d4 fire damage if handled barehanded. Unproficient foragers take the damage automatically on harvest.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Fire Stalk
unidentified.description: A bright orange-capped mushroom growing from cracked volcanic rock near a steaming vent. Warm to the touch, and bare skin contact leaves a stinging sensation.

items.name: Hoshi no Kona 星の粉 (Star Dust) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Hoshi no Kona 星の粉 (Star Dust)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Stable for weeks in sealed stone vessel; exposure to open air fades the resonance
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); brush and seal-able container
Restrictions: Only forms during Hikarishō when dragon auroras touch the plateau
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A fine, glittering powder found on exposed surfaces of the Hoshimori Plateau during the peak of Hikarishō, when the dragon auroras touch the ground. The powder is warm, faintly luminescent, and dissolves completely into food. The flavor is impossible to describe in conventional terms — those who have tasted it say it changes every time, and that the meal it seasons feels significant in a way ordinary food does not.

DM Notes

**Event-gated:** Hikarishō. Seimaster interest from Hoshimori.

items.name: Hoshi-take 星茸 (Star Cap) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Hoshi-take 星茸 (Star Cap)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Withers by dawn; no reliable preservation method known
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); astronomical knowledge; seimaster guidance
Restrictions: Appears only during rare triple-star alignments over the Hoshimori Plateau
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A tiny, brilliantly luminescent mushroom found on the Hoshimori Plateau during specific stellar alignments. The caps are no larger than a thumbnail and glow with a light that shifts through the spectrum — gold, blue, red, violet — mirroring the three-star system overhead. They appear in clusters and vanish by dawn. The taste is indescribable. Seimasters at Hoshimori have attempted to study them for decades without satisfactory results.

DM Notes

**Astronomical event-gated.** Tie to the Ryushinki alignment or lesser conjunctions. Possible plot-hook material for Hoshimori seimaster quests.

unidentified.description: A tiny thumbnail-sized mushroom cap glowing with light that shifts through gold, blue, red, and violet under an open night sky.

Hoshikusa 星草 (Star Grass)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 1 day fresh; loses luminescence immediately on drying
Tools: Herbalism kit; presence at Hoshimori during Hikarishō
Restrictions: Hikarishō only — hours-long harvest window
Grade: 並 Nami (craft modifier: -2)

A luminescent grass found only on the Hoshimori Plateau during specific celestial alignments — when Ryūgetsu enters full phase and the aurora of Hikarishō touches the ground. The blades glow with a shifting, opalescent light and are warm to the touch. The window for harvesting is narrow — hours at most. When used in cooking, it imparts a sensation that defies description: a warmth that feels like being watched over.

DM Notes

Harvesting requires being physically present at the plateau during Hikarishō — a campaign event, not a routine foraging opportunity.

items.name: Hoshiyo-jio 星夜塩 (Starlit Salt) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Hoshiyo-jio 星夜塩 (Starlit Salt)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Hoshimori observatory tradition — gifted
Preservation: Stable indefinitely in sealed crystal
Tools: None
Restrictions: Produced only by Hoshimori observatory communities during Hikarishō
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A salt evaporated under the Hoshimori aurora during the peak of Hikarishō, when the dragon auroras touch the ground. The process takes an entire season and can only be completed by the observatory communities of Sora, who time their pans to the celestial alignments with instruments older than any living seimaster. The finished crystals glow faintly in darkness and carry a flavour that shifts with the stars overhead. Used only in the most extraordinary meals — once in a lifetime, if at all.

DM Notes

Seimaster-observatory gift. Tied to Ryushinki lore. --- **Yama-no-Ōkami (Mountain God) — Named Beast Harvest (Shushoku)** The Yama-no-Ōkami harvest additionally yielded one Shushoku-category component — the rendered subcutaneous fat. All Yama-no-Ōkami harvests are locked at 極上 Gokujō (the nat-20 harvest check during the Fushichō ashfall). See Part II "Named Beast Harvests" for the full harvest record.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Starlit Salt
unidentified.description: Faintly luminous salt crystals that seem to hold a memory of distant starlight.

items.name: Inochi no Shio 命の塩 (Salt of Life) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Inochi no Shio 命の塩 (Salt of Life)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Harvested (Saishū)
Preservation: Self-replenishing at the deposit; stable indefinitely once harvested
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); Arcana (Int) DC 15; clean stone vessel
Restrictions: Over-harvest depletes site for years. Less than a dozen sites known.
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A crystalline substance found at the exact point where sei-active spring water meets volcanic mineral deposits — a convergence so specific that fewer than a dozen sites in all of Kagekuni produce it. The crystals form slowly and are self-replenishing, but harvesting too aggressively depletes the site for years. The flavor is warmth, vitality, and something that sits beyond the tongue's ability to categorize. Meals seasoned with it produce effects that border on the miraculous.

DM Notes

**Sacred / ecological gate.** Over-harvest has in-world consequences. Associate with restoration/healing recipes.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Salt of Life
unidentified.description: A warm, softly alive crystal from where hot spring meets volcanic mineral vent, faintly pulsing in the hand.

items.name: Inoshishi 猪 (Wild Boar) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Inoshishi 猪 (Wild Boar)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 2 days fresh; indefinitely if smoked or salted
Tools: Spear, polearm, or bow; cook's utensils for butchery
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Dense, dark, heavily marbled meat from Hokori's wild boars. The flavour is strong and distinctly gamey — deeper than venison, sweeter than bear — and the fat carries the diet of the forest: pine nut, fallen fruit, and fungus. Stewed with miso it becomes the defining winter meal of mountain communities.

DM Notes

Dangerous to hunt — a wounded boar can kill a man before dying. Winter boar is considered the finest, the fat layer at its thickest after the autumn foraging. A successful boar hunt yields Kegawa (hide) and Hone (tusks) as secondary materials.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Wild Boar
unidentified.description: Heavy, dark-red cuts of large-game meat with thick marbled fat — noticeably stronger in smell than common game.

items.name: Ishinage

description.value:
Description

A braided cord sling for hurling stones, the ishinage is the weapon of shepherds, mountain villagers, and anyone too poor for a bow. Ammunition is as close as the nearest riverbed. Skilled slingers can crack bone at impressive range, and in the highlands of Kaze province, ishinage tournaments are a village tradition. It weighs nothing, costs nothing, and has been killing since before steel was forged.

items.name: Iwa-ninniku 岩大蒜 (Cliff Garlic) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Iwa-ninniku 岩大蒜 (Cliff Garlic)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 14 days fresh; indefinitely dried
Tools: Herbalism kit; climbing gear often required
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A pungent wild garlic variant that grows from cracks in cliff faces and exposed rock. Stronger than lowland nobiru — the flavour is sharp, almost medicinal, and lingers for hours. Mountain villagers in Sora use it as both seasoning and folk remedy. Harvesting requires climbing or reaching into awkward crevices.

DM Notes

Sora villagers consider it a better remedy than lowland garlic — stronger, cleaner, and said to ward against mountain sickness.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Cliff Garlic
unidentified.description: Small tight bulbs pulled from a rock crack, smelling overwhelmingly of garlic and something faintly mineral.

items.name: Iwana 岩魚 (Mountain Char) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Iwana 岩魚 (Mountain Char)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 1 day fresh; 10 days salted; indefinitely smoked
Tools: Fishing tackle; spears in shallow water
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

The hardy freshwater char of cold mountain streams. The flesh is pale pink and the flavour carries the sharp cleanness of glacial water and the resinous trace of upstream conifers. Salt-grilled whole over charcoal, the skin crisps and the belly fat melts into something mountain hermits consider a perfect meal.

DM Notes

Traditional catch of mountain ascetics and hermit monks. Streamside cooking over a small fire is considered the only proper preparation.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Mountain Char
unidentified.description: A sleek dark-green fish the length of a forearm, pale-bellied, with scattered red spots along the flanks.

items.name: Iwashi 鰯 (Sardine) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Iwashi 鰯 (Sardine)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Common
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 1 day fresh; 30 days salted; indefinitely dried
Tools: Nets; fishing tackle for rod-and-line work
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Small silver ocean fish that run in vast schools along Hokori's coasts. The flesh is oily and strong-flavoured — hated by some, beloved by others. Grilled on a metal plate over coals until the skin crisps and the bones soften, they are the humble backbone of coastal Mizu and Nami kitchens.

DM Notes

The anchor ingredient of coastal peasant cuisine. A good haul from a beach-seine can yield enough to feed a village and leave a surplus for drying.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Sardine
unidentified.description: Handfuls of small silver-blue fish, each no longer than a finger, packed tightly together and carrying a strong oceanic smell.

The anchor ingredient of coastal peasant cuisine. A good haul from a beach-seine can yield enough to feed a village and leave a surplus for drying.

Upscale noble item. Grade represents brewery prestige.

items.name: Kaen-su 火炎酢 (Flame Vinegar) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kaen-su 火炎酢 (Flame Vinegar)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Harvested (Saishū, thermal)
Preservation: Indefinite in sealed vessel; stable
Tools: Herbalism kit or alchemy kit (advantage); heat-resistant collection vessel
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A pungent vinegar produced naturally in thermal pools of Hi province where specific mineral concentrations and bacterial colonies create an acidic brine. The liquid is collected from shallow depressions near volcanic vents — it tastes of heat, stone, and a sharp acidity that cuts through the richest meat. Cannot be replicated outside its volcanic source.

DM Notes

Hi-province-only. Harvesting in active thermal zones may require a Con save on failure.

unidentified.description: A sharp, pungent liquid collected from a shallow thermal pool, faintly warm to the touch with a mineral smell.

items.name: Kagami Mochi no Shinsei 鏡餅の神聖 (Sacred Mirror Mochi) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kagami Mochi no Shinsei 鏡餅の神聖 (Sacred Mirror Mochi)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Ceremonial distribution only
Preservation: Remains ritually potent for the year; edible for months
Tools: None
Restrictions: Distributed once per year at shrines; mortal travellers almost never receive it
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Ceremonial mochi prepared once per year at specific Shinto shrines during the turning of the year. The rice is pounded by priests in ritual silence, and the finished mochi is placed upon the shrine altar for seven days before being divided among the shrine community. Those who receive a piece are said to be blessed by the ancestors for the year to come. Mortal travellers almost never obtain it; when they do, it is because a priest has chosen to honour them specifically.

DM Notes

**Ancestor-blessing hook.** Annual distribution.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Sacred Mirror Mochi
unidentified.description: A small white mochi piece wrapped in sacred paper bearing a shrine seal.

description.value:
Kagerō-sō 蜻蛉草 (Shimmer Herb)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 5 days fresh; indefinitely dried
Tools: Herbalism kit
Restrictions: Narrow geographic range
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A low, ground-hugging herb found along the banks of the Kagerō River in Kaze province, identifiable by the faint shimmer on its leaves that mirrors the river's thermal haze. The leaves have a complex, slightly numbing quality that enhances other flavours when used in small amounts. Overuse deadens the palate.

DM Notes

Enhancement, not flavour of its own. A pinch in a broth raises the other ingredients; too much kills the meal outright.

items.name: Kama

description.value:
Description

A short-handled sickle with a curved blade originally designed for harvesting rice, the kama became a weapon of necessity for farmers forbidden to carry swords. Paired kama in trained hands can hook weapons, catch limbs, and deliver quick slashing cuts. Burakumin communities have developed their own fighting traditions around this humble tool.

items.name: Kaminari-kusa 雷草 (Thunder Herb) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kaminari-kusa 雷草 (Thunder Herb)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 1 day fresh; 14 days carefully dried
Tools: Herbalism kit; storm survival
Restrictions: Must be harvested during active thunderstorm on exposed ridgeline — dangerous
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Found only during active thunderstorms on exposed ridgelines — the herb appears to sprout from bare rock in the minutes following a lightning strike and withers within the hour. The leaves crackle faintly when touched and carry a sharp, ozone-like scent. Harvesting requires being on an exposed ridgeline during a thunderstorm, which is exactly as dangerous as it sounds.

DM Notes

Harvesting is a scene, not a roll. If a character attempts it during an actual storm, require a saving throw against a lightning strike (DC 15 Dexterity, 4d10 lightning on failure) before they can even make the forage check. ---

unidentified.name: Unidentified Thunder Herb
unidentified.description: Small sharp leaves that crackle faintly with static when handled, smelling of rain and lightning.

items.name: Kamo 鴨 (Wild Duck) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kamo 鴨 (Wild Duck)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 2 days fresh; 14 days salted
Tools: Bow, net, or sling; cook's utensils for dressing
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Rich dark meat from the wild ducks that winter on Kagekuni's wetlands. The breast is layered with golden fat beneath dark rose flesh; the legs render for long braising. Duck in Hokori is traditionally paired with negi (leek) and a clear, savoury broth.

The duck runs are among the defining hunts of late autumn in the lowland provinces. A skilled bowman working a morning flight can fill a pack in an hour.

items.name: Kanabo

description.value:
Description

A massive club of iron-studded hardwood — or solid iron in the hands of the strongest warriors — the kanabo is a weapon of raw, crushing power. Folk tales associate it with oni, the ogre-demons who wield tree-trunk versions, and warriors who carry one earn wary respect. Guhuza and other large-framed fighters favor it for breaking shield walls and splintering armor.

items.name: Kanamuchi

description.value:
Description

An iron-headed mace with a flanged or faceted striking surface, carried primarily by sohei warrior-monks who consider edged weapons spiritually impure for their order. The kanamuchi channels blunt force through a short haft, crumpling armor without drawing blood. Temple guardians and traveling monks favor it as a weapon that incapacitates rather than kills.

Broad, deep-green leaves with a sharp peppery bite that mellows with cooking. Self-seeds along cultivated field margins and disturbed ground, especially in Tsuchi and Hana where farmers allow them to grow wild between plantings. Used in pickles, stir-fries, and the spicy soups of winter.

Abundant between plantings in the rice provinces. A reliable supplement when other greens are out of season. --- **Uncommon**

items.name: Kaseki-gani 化石蟹 (Fossil Crab) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kaseki-gani 化石蟹 (Fossil Crab)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged
Preservation: Must be kept alive until cooking; dead crab spoils within hours
Tools: None — hand-caught; cook's utensils essential for cracking the stone-like shell
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A deep-shelled crab so ancient in lineage that its carapace is nearly as hard as stone, mineralised by millennia of selection for defence. The flesh inside is astonishing — dense, sweet, and faintly floral, with a texture closer to dense custard than to ordinary crab. Breaking the shell takes a stone hammer; the reward is worth the labour.

DM Notes

Rarely encountered — a successful forage is a small event. Most often found by foragers working unusual stretches of coastline, particularly where tidal pools sit against ancient volcanic rock.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Fossil Crab
unidentified.description: A dark, rock-like crab whose carapace could be mistaken for a wet stone — until it moves. Improbably heavy for its size.

items.name: Kaseki-take 化石茸 (Fossil Shelf) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kaseki-take 化石茸 (Fossil Shelf)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Nearly indefinite; dense flesh resists rot
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); sharp tool for harvesting dense flesh
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A large, shelf-like fungus found growing on petrified wood in ancient geological formations — the Buried Road of Tsuchi, the deep foundations of Progenitor ruins, and exposed strata in river gorges. The flesh is incredibly dense and must be thinly sliced. The flavor is deep, complex, and ancient-tasting in a way that is difficult to articulate — like stone dust and old libraries and deep time.

DM Notes

Often found in ancient sites — use as a proximity signal for archaeological discovery. --- **極上 Gokujō — Very Rare**

unidentified.name: Unidentified Fossil Shelf
unidentified.description: A dense, stone-hard shelf fungus on a petrified log, almost mineral to the touch, weighing far more than it looks.

items.name: Kasumi-sō 霞草 (Mist Herb) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kasumi-sō 霞草 (Mist Herb)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 5 days fresh; indefinitely dried
Tools: Herbalism kit
Restrictions: Concentrated in Kaze fog zones
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Found only in the dense fog banks of Kaze province's deepest valleys, where visibility drops to arm's length and sound arrives from the wrong direction. The herb is identifiable by scent alone — a sharp green fragrance that cuts through the ambient dampness. Used in cooking, it produces a heightened clarity of taste in other ingredients, as though the fog around one's senses had been lifted.

DM Notes

Finding it at all requires a Wisdom (Perception) check or equivalent — disadvantage if the character is relying on sight. --- **Very Rare**

unidentified.name: Unidentified Mist Herb
unidentified.description: Small pale leaves that can only be found by scent — the sharp green fragrance is distinctive even in thick fog.

items.name: Katana

description.value:
Description

A single-edged longsword with a gentle curve and a long two-handed grip. The blade is forged from folded steel and bears the maker's mark near the hilt. In Kagekuni, the katana is more than a weapon — it is the soul of the samurai who carries it.

items.name: Katsuobushi 鰹節 (Dried Bonito Flakes) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Katsuobushi 鰹節 (Dried Bonito Flakes)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: Common
Source: Traded (smoked/dried)
Preservation: Keeps a year in sealed packet; flakes soften with humidity
Tools: None
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Smoked, dried, and shaved skipjack tuna, sold in paper packets of paper-thin flakes. Distinct from dried dashi blocks — katsuobushi is used as a finishing topping on hot food, where the flakes curl and "dance" in the rising steam as though the fish were alive again. A cornerstone of Mizu and Nami cooking and the defining flavour of ocean-touched cuisine.

DM Notes

Classic "dancing flakes" moment for evocative dish descriptions.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Dried Bonito Flakes
unidentified.description: Paper-thin pale-brown flakes that curl and shimmer when scattered over hot food.

items.name: Kawa-gani 川蟹 (River Crab) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kawa-gani 川蟹 (River Crab)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Common
Source: Hunted
Preservation: Must be kept alive until cooking; cooked meat keeps 1 day
Tools: None (hand-caught); cook's utensils for dressing
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Small freshwater crabs pulled from clear streams and the edges of rice paddies. The shells are dark mottled green in life, turning vivid orange when cooked. Sweet, briny flesh inside a shell that must be cracked with fingers or the butt of a knife. Grilled whole, their flavour intensifies into something far greater than their size suggests.

DM Notes

Gathered by hand from clear streams and paddy margins. Peasant children often harvest them as a side activity during other work. Fishing tackle not required. Best yields immediately after rainfall.

unidentified.name: Unidentified River Crab
unidentified.description: Small armored arthropods, palm-sized, with dark mottled shells and pincers held defensively. They clack faintly when disturbed.

Tools: None (hand-caught); cook's utensils for dressing
Grade: 特上 Tokujō (craft modifier: +2)

Small freshwater crabs pulled from clear streams and the edges of rice paddies. The shells are dark mottled green in life, turning vivid orange when cooked. Sweet, briny flesh inside a shell that must be cracked with fingers or the butt of a knife. Grilled whole, their flavour intensifies into something far greater than their size suggests.

DM Notes

Gathered by hand from clear streams and paddy margins. Peasant children often harvest them as a side activity during other work. Fishing tackle not required. Best yields immediately after rainfall.

items.name: Kazan-koshō 火山胡椒 (Volcano Pepper) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kazan-koshō 火山胡椒 (Volcano Pepper)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Dried indefinitely; oil extract 6 months
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); **mildly toxic — alchemy kit to handle safely**
Restrictions: Enshiyama is an active volcanic hazard
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

The fruit of a stunted bush that grows in the ash fields surrounding Enshiyama's crater, where soil temperatures remain elevated year-round. The berries are tiny and dark red, and the heat they carry is unlike any other pepper — it builds slowly, reaches an almost painful intensity, then subsides into a deep, smoky warmth. Hi province alchemists classify it as mildly toxic. Hi province cooks classify anyone who can't handle it as weak.

DM Notes

**Mild toxicity:** unproficient handlers take 1 poison damage per berry eaten above reasonable dose.

items.name: Kinryūgoi 金竜鯉 (Golden Dragon Carp) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kinryūgoi 金竜鯉 (Golden Dragon Carp)

Category: Niku
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 1 day fresh; loses its properties if preserved
Tools: Fishing tackle of master quality; traditionally hand-caught by a fisher with Wisdom (Survival) expertise
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

The legendary golden-scaled carp of the Kinryūgawa — a fish said to carry a fragment of the Golden Dragon's essence in its flesh. Those who have eaten it describe it as the most complete meal of their life — every element of taste layered through the single fish. Even a small portion is a meal worth travelling to.

DM Notes

A single Kinryūgoi kill is a life-defining event for a fisher. Tradition holds that the fish appears only to those whose intent matches the dragon's favour. See Part II — Named Beast Harvests for ritual obligations around the catch. --- **Named Beast Harvests — Yama-no-Ōkami (Mountain God of the Tenchūsan Ren)** *Slain in the mountain pass during the Fushichō ashfall. A Huge-category beast — roughly twelve to fifteen feet from nose to haunch, eight feet at the shoulder, and weighing somewhere between six and eight thousand pounds. Butchered with exceptional skill — the natural 20 on the harvest check triggered the bonus d10 and cleared the Legendary threshold, securing every cut the beast had to offer, including the Reikokoro. All food components from this harvest are tagged at 極上 Gokujō grade by virtue of the harvest roll. The Reikokoro is a single-grade Legendary exception and does not carry the standard four-grade variant block.*

unidentified.name: Unidentified Golden Dragon Carp
unidentified.description: A large carp with metallic-gold scales that catch light like polished brass. Impossibly heavy for its size. The eyes remain bright and the flesh faintly warm long after death.

description.value:
Kinuo 絹魚 (Silkfish)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 1 day fresh; 7 days salted
Tools: Fishing tackle with fine line; nets are too coarse
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Slender, almost translucent fish from cold mountain streams, so pale that they are nearly invisible against a sand bottom. The flesh is delicate and silky in texture — the flavour is clean and cold, like the water itself — and the smallest overcooking turns them to paper. A test of a fisher-cook's patience.

DM Notes

A delicacy of mountain-stream cuisine. Fished with the finest tackle; rough handling destroys the product. Sora and upper Kaze are the canonical sources.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Silkfish
unidentified.description: Translucent silver-white fish the length of a hand, fragile enough that a rough grip could snap one. Almost no scent.

items.name: Kodachi

description.value:
Description

A shorter, lighter variant of the katana with a blade under two feet, the kodachi occupies the space between wakizashi and full-length sword. Its compact size and excellent balance make it ideal for indoor fighting, narrow corridors, and the quick thrust-and-parry style favored by courtiers and duelists. Where a katana commands respect through presence, a kodachi earns it through speed.

items.name: Koikuchi-shōyu 濃口醤油 (Dark Soy Paste) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Koikuchi-shōyu 濃口醤油 (Dark Soy Paste)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Traded (aged ferment)
Preservation: Years in sealed wooden cask fragment
Tools: None
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A deeper, more intense soy paste aged longer than common shōyu, with a darker colour and a more complex, almost smoky flavour profile. Used as a finishing sauce or in glazes where the depth of flavour matters more than the volume applied. Aged at least two years in wooden casks before being drawn off and bottled. A single drop on grilled fish shows the difference immediately.

DM Notes

Finishing sauce — used sparingly in refined cooking.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Dark Soy Paste
unidentified.description: An almost-black soy sauce in a wooden-stoppered flask, thicker and richer than common shōyu.

description.value:
Kōji 麹 (Rice Mold Starter)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Traded (cultured)
Preservation: Active culture, needs cool dry storage; viable weeks
Tools: Brewing / fermentation knowledge to use
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A live fermentation culture — rice grains inoculated with the kōji mold that enables the production of sake, miso, shōyu, and countless other foods. Sold in small cloth-wrapped bundles by fermentation masters, who guard their specific strains carefully. A traveller with kōji, rice, and a few weeks can brew their own sake, miso, or pickles on the road — the beginning of a long and patient art.

DM Notes

Downtime brewing lever. --- **特上 Tokujō — Rare**

items.name: Kome 米 (Rice) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kome 米 (Rice)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: Common
Source: Traded (cultivated)
Preservation: Keeps months in dry cloth; years if properly stored in sealed containers
Tools: None
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

The foundation of nearly every meal in Kagekuni. White polished rice is carried by all travellers in small cloth bags and purchased in any settlement. Peasant households stretch it with brown rice or mixed grains; samurai eat it white. Quality varies subtly by province — Tsuchi rice is said to be the finest for daily eating, while Kusa's slightly sweeter grain is favoured for festival dishes. A traveller without kome in their pack is a traveller who expects hospitality.

DM Notes

The default staple. Never run out of this in a market town.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Rice
unidentified.description: A small cloth bag of clean white polished grains, heavy for its size.

items.name: Konsaibo

description.value:
Description

A short wooden club reinforced with iron studs or wrapped in cord for a better grip. Konsaibo are carried by doshin — low-ranking police officers — to subdue criminals without killing, and by peasants who cannot afford forged steel. Cheap, effective, and requiring no training to swing, they are the most common weapon in Kagekuni's lower castes.

items.name: Kōri-iwana 氷岩魚 (Ice Char) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kōri-iwana 氷岩魚 (Ice Char)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Rare
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 1 day fresh; indefinitely frozen in mountain cold
Tools: Ice-fishing tackle; a spear through a cut hole works as well
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A winter variant of the mountain char, caught only through the ice of frozen Kōri-no-Mori streams and high-altitude lakes. The flesh is pale pink verging on white, with a concentrated, almost sweet flavour that no warm-water fish can match. Traditionally sliced thin and served raw when fresh — the cold water produces a cleanliness no cooking could improve upon.

DM Notes

The peak catch of mountain winter fishing. Traditional Kōri-no-Mori villages have an entire ritual vocabulary around ice-char fishing that predates the formal Shinto calendar. --- **Very Rare**

unidentified.name: Unidentified Ice Char
unidentified.description: A sleek pale fish still cool to the touch, its flesh unusually firm, its eyes bright even after death.

items.name: Koteppo

description.value:
Description

A compact matchlock pistol small enough to fire with one hand, the koteppo sacrifices range and stopping power for concealability. Developed by Glimfyr gunsmiths on Tatara and smuggled into the mainland despite Teppo Bugyo regulations, it is prized by bodyguards, spies, and anyone who needs a hidden weapon that ends arguments instantly at close range. The thunderclap of its discharge makes stealth impossible afterward.

items.name: Kōtetsu-take 鋼茸 (Steel Cap) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kōtetsu-take 鋼茸 (Steel Cap)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Stable for months; dries well; mineral content intensifies
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); mining pick recommended for extraction from mineral crust
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A dark, metallic-capped mushroom found in the iron-rich soil around Kurogane Yama and the mining settlements of Tsuchi. The cap has a genuine metallic sheen and the flesh contains trace minerals that give it a faintly ferrous taste. Miners consider them good luck. Alchemists value them for the mineral content.

DM Notes

Tsuchi regional signature. Miner superstition — good omen loot.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Steel Cap
unidentified.description: A dark mushroom with a metallic-seeming cap growing in iron-stained soil near an old mine tailing.

items.name: Kozuchi

description.value:
Description

A small hammer with a compact iron head and a short wooden handle, the kozuchi is the universal tool of Kagekuni's smiths, carpenters, and stonemasons. Zirak artisans on Tatara carry finely balanced versions that serve equally well for riveting armor plates or caving in a skull. The name literally means "small hammer," and many a craftsman has defended their workshop with one.

items.name: Kumo-no-Su Kōji 雲の巣麹 (Cloud Nest Mold) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kumo-no-Su Kōji 雲の巣麹 (Cloud Nest Mold)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Foraged (Saishū) — traditional communities
Preservation: Must be stored in dry cold; active culture remains viable for months
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); clean collecting surface; Sora community permission
Restrictions: Sora villages guard specific strains; outsider collection without permission is theft
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A beneficial mold culture found growing on grain stores in the high-altitude settlements of Sora, where the cold, dry air and altitude produce unique fermentation conditions. The mold is collected and used to inoculate rice for a distinctively sharp, clean sake and a fermented seasoning paste with an almost effervescent quality. The communities of Kumo-no-Ue guard their specific culture strains carefully.

DM Notes

Social/political obstacle — Sora communities grant strains only as gifts of honour.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Cloud Nest Mold
unidentified.description: A pale, fuzzy mold culture clinging to a grain of polished rice, dry and almost crystalline in appearance.

items.name: Kumokiji 雲雉 (Cloud Pheasant) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kumokiji 雲雉 (Cloud Pheasant)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Rare
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 2 days fresh; 14 days salted
Tools: Bow with strong draw; the bird is wary and high-flying
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A large, crested pheasant that lives above the cloud ceiling of the Hoshimori Plateau and the higher peaks. The breast meat is pale, tender, and carries an impossibly clean flavour — something the people of Kumo-no-Ue describe as "the taste of thin air." Tradition holds the bird only descends to lower altitudes during Hikarishō.

DM Notes

The Hoshimori observatories guard their hunting privileges jealously. Seimasters sometimes receive a cloud-pheasant breast as ceremonial payment.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Cloud Pheasant
unidentified.description: A large plucked game bird with ivory-pale flesh and a few white-barred feathers still attached. The body is cool to the touch even hours after kill.

items.name: Kumokiji 雲雉 (Cloud Pheasant) (並 Nami)

description.value:
Kumokiji 雲雉 (Cloud Pheasant)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Rare
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 2 days fresh; 14 days salted
Tools: Bow with strong draw; the bird is wary and high-flying
Grade: 並 Nami (craft modifier: -2)

A large, crested pheasant that lives above the cloud ceiling of the Hoshimori Plateau and the higher peaks. The breast meat is pale, tender, and carries an impossibly clean flavour — something the people of Kumo-no-Ue describe as "the taste of thin air." Tradition holds the bird only descends to lower altitudes during Hikarishō.

DM Notes

The Hoshimori observatories guard their hunting privileges jealously. Seimasters sometimes receive a cloud-pheasant breast as ceremonial payment.

items.name: Kurenai-take 紅茸 (Crimson Cap) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kurenai-take 紅茸 (Crimson Cap)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Fresh 2–3 days; dries well; holds aromatic warmth
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); **knowledge of gill colour is lethally important**
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A brilliant red-capped mushroom found near hot springs and thermal vents in Hi province. Easily mistaken for a poisonous variety — only those who know the distinguishing underside pattern (pale gold gills rather than white) should pick them. The flavor is rich, almost smoky, with a warmth that reflects its volcanic habitat.

DM Notes

**Risk flag:** unproficient forager who attempts identification should roll with disadvantage. Failed identification by grade-0 forager may yield poisonous lookalike.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Crimson Cap
unidentified.description: A brilliant red-capped mushroom growing in warm soil near a thermal vent, the underside hidden.

Kurokaze-sō 黒風草 (Black Wind Herb)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 5 days fresh; indefinitely dried
Tools: Herbalism kit
Restrictions: Found only in Kaze province
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A dark-leafed herb found only in Kaze province, growing in the shadow of black pines where the mist never fully lifts. Used by Gekkō-trained herbalists for alertness tinctures. Bitter, with a sharp aftertaste that clears the head.

DM Notes

The Gekkō clan's herbalist lineage catalogued this plant extensively — a character with the right contacts can learn the formal tincture preparation.

items.name: Kuroyō-su 黒曜酢 (Obsidian Vinegar) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Kuroyō-su 黒曜酢 (Obsidian Vinegar)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: Rare
Source: Harvested (Saishū)
Preservation: Stable indefinitely
Tools: Alchemy kit (advantage); heat-resistant vessel
Restrictions: Obsidian Fields are hazardous terrain
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A naturally occurring acidic mineral brine found seeping through obsidian formations in the Kurosō fields of Hi province. The liquid is dark, almost black, and carries a sharp acidity with an underlying smokiness. Alchemists use it as a reagent; cooks use it — very sparingly — as a finishing acid that adds complexity no other vinegar can match.

DM Notes

Alchemist reagent and finishing acid.

items.name: Kusarigama

description.value:
Description

A kama sickle attached to a weighted chain, the kusarigama is a weapon born from peasant ingenuity. The wielder swings the weighted end to entangle weapons or limbs, then closes with the sickle blade. Its reach and unpredictable attack angles make it surprisingly effective against swordsmen, and it can be disguised as ordinary farming equipment. Rebel groups and covert operatives favor it for this reason.

items.name: Maitake 舞茸 (Hen of the Woods) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Maitake 舞茸 (Hen of the Woods)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Dries very well; trimmings keep on the road
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); knife for cleaning
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Large, ruffled clusters found at the base of old oak and chestnut trees, growing in tiered layers that can weigh several pounds each. The flavour is earthy and deep with a subtle peppery finish. Prized in autumn cooking — a single find can feed a party twice over, and the dried trimmings keep well on the road. Considered a lucky discovery by foragers.

DM Notes

A "lucky find" narrative callout — reward for thorough autumn foraging.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Hen of the Woods
unidentified.description: A massive ruffled cluster of overlapping grey-brown fronds at the base of an old hardwood tree, tiered layers of fan-like caps resembling a roosting hen.

items.name: Masakari

description.value:
Description

A broad-bladed war axe with a crescent cutting edge and a stout wooden haft, the masakari is the weapon of mountain warriors and militant sohei orders. Heavier and more deliberate than the woodsman's ono, it is designed to split armor and shields. Wielded in one hand with a shield or in two for devastating overhead chops, the masakari rewards strength over finesse.

items.name: Matsutake 松茸 (Pine Mushroom) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Matsutake 松茸 (Pine Mushroom)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Fresh 3–4 days; dries adequately; aroma fades quickly
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); patience and dry hillsides
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Large, thick-stemmed mushrooms found under red pine trees in well-drained soil. The aroma is distinctive — a spicy, almost cinnamon-like fragrance that announces a find before you see it. Highly prized and seasonal — autumn only. Despite the prestige, they are common enough in the right terrain to be found by a patient forager.

DM Notes

Autumn-locked. Common in the right terrain, but the terrain is narrow.

items.name: Mirin 味醂 (Sweet Rice Wine) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Mirin 味醂 (Sweet Rice Wine)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: Common
Source: Traded (brewed)
Preservation: Indefinite in sealed flask
Tools: None
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Sweet rice wine used exclusively for cooking, never for drinking. Mirin produces the characteristic glossy glaze on grilled fish and braised meats, and adds a subtle sweetness that refined sugar cannot replicate. Sold in small corked flasks in every market town — a small splash is enough to transform a simple glaze into something worth remembering.

DM Notes

Glaze essential. Standard upgrade item for dishes.

Preservation: Indefinite in sealed flask
Tools: None
Grade: 特上 Tokujō (craft modifier: +2)

Sweet rice wine used exclusively for cooking, never for drinking. Mirin produces the characteristic glossy glaze on grilled fish and braised meats, and adds a subtle sweetness that refined sugar cannot replicate. Sold in small corked flasks in every market town — a small splash is enough to transform a simple glaze into something worth remembering.

Glaze essential. Standard upgrade item for dishes.

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 2 days fresh; loses flavour when dried

Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A deep-green aquatic plant found in the clearest, coldest springs fed by snowmelt from the Tenchūsan Ren. Must be harvested underwater.

Harvesting requires reaching into painfully cold water — a character without cold protection may need a Constitution save for extended work.

Murasaki-ha 紫葉 (Purple Leaf)

Category: Yakuso

Source: Foraged
Preservation: 5 days fresh; indefinitely dried (loses colour)
Tools: Herbalism kit
Restrictions: Endemic to Kusa province
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A broad-leafed plant endemic to Kusa's lowland forests, where it grows in the violet grass meadows alongside the native murasaki-gusa. The leaves are a deep purple-black and have a mild, earthy sweetness that complements rich meats. Kusa cooks wrap fish and game in the leaves before steaming — a regional technique unknown outside the province.

DM Notes

The wrap-and-steam technique is part of the distinctive cuisine of the Murasaki-hara and unknown outside Kusa — a chef from elsewhere would need instruction.

items.name: Nagamaki

description.value:
Description

A long-bladed weapon with an extended grip wrapped in cord, blurring the line between sword and polearm. The nagamaki's balance point sits near the middle of its total length, allowing powerful chopping strikes with the leverage of a two-handed grip while maintaining the cutting geometry of a sword blade. Versatile warriors prize it for its ability to control space on a crowded battlefield.

items.name: Nagayari

description.value:
Description

An extremely long spear — sometimes exceeding twenty feet — the nagayari is a formation weapon, not an individual one. Rows of ashigaru brace nagayari in dense hedgehog formations that no cavalry can penetrate. Individually the weapon is cumbersome and nearly useless in close quarters, but in disciplined ranks it creates an impenetrable wall of steel points. Entire battles have been won by the side with longer spears.

items.name: Nageya

description.value:
Description

A light throwing spear with a narrow leaf-shaped head, the nageya is issued to ashigaru infantry for volley fire before melee engagement. Cheaper than arrows and requiring less training than a bow, bundles of nageya are stockpiled in every garrison. Hunters also use them for bringing down game at medium range.

items.name: Naginata

description.value:
Description

A curved blade mounted on a long wooden shaft, the naginata combines the reach of a spear with the cutting power of a sword. It is the traditional weapon of onna-bugeisha — female warriors — and temple defenders, though any warrior who values reach adopts it gladly. The sweeping arc of a naginata strike can cut through multiple enemies in a single motion, making it devastating against lightly armored opponents.

items.name: Nameko 滑子 (Amber Cap) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Nameko 滑子 (Amber Cap)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Must be cooked or dried within 1 day; dries well; fresh keeps 1–2 days only
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage)
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Small, glossy, button-sized mushrooms found in clusters on decaying wood in damp forests. The caps are coated in a natural glaze that gives them a wet-amber sheen even in full sun. The flavor is mild and slightly nutty, and the slick texture is prized in soups and stews where it adds body to the broth.

DM Notes

Commonly paired with miso for soup base. Foragers learn them early.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Amber Cap
unidentified.description: Small button-shaped mushrooms in a tight cluster on damp decaying wood, caps coated in what looks like a natural lacquer.

description.value:
Nami no Hana 波の花 (Wave Blossom)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Harvested (Saishū, coastal) — seasonal
Preservation: Dried 3–4 months; humidity destroys it
Tools: Knife or fine brush; storm-timing knowledge
Restrictions: Only forms during Tatsunami (extreme four-moon tide event)
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A dried sea foam that crystallizes on coastal rocks during the height of Tatsunami season, when the four-moon alignment drives extreme tides. The crystals are white, feathery, and dissolve on the tongue with an intense brininess followed by an unexpected sweetness. Used as a finishing salt on delicate dishes. Available only during a narrow seasonal window.

items.name: Nodachi

description.value:
Description

An oversized katana with a blade exceeding three feet, the nodachi is a battlefield weapon designed for sweeping cuts against cavalry and massed infantry. Too long to draw from a hip scabbard, it is carried slung across the back or held ready in both hands. Elite foot soldiers who wield it stride ahead of formations, using the blade's enormous reach to break enemy lines before the yari walls close.

items.name: Odeppo

description.value:
Description

A heavy matchlock musket with a long barrel and a forked rest for stability, the odeppo delivers devastating firepower at extended range. Too heavy and slow-loading for mobile warfare, it is deployed from castle walls, behind fortifications, and in prepared ambush positions. Zirak engineers developed the design for penetrating heavy armor at siege distances; a single ball can punch through a wooden shield and the warrior behind it.

items.name: Ōkami-niku 狼肉 (Mountain God's Flesh)

description.value:
Ōkami-niku 狼肉 (Mountain God's Flesh)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: One-Time (Yama-no-Ōkami harvest)
Preservation: 3 days fresh; indefinitely if smoked or salted
Tools: Butcher's or cook's utensils (already harvested)
Restrictions: One-time only; no further supply possible

Dense, dark-grained muscle from the shoulders and haunches of a mountain god, marbled with winter fat and deeply flavoured from a lifetime of predation at altitude. The meat carries a faint mineral tang — cold stone and pine smoke — that no ordinary game possesses. Cooks well in almost any preparation, though the flavour is strong enough to overpower delicate seasonings.

DM Notes

See `dm/campaign-state.md` for current inventory tracking. Meat retains the cold touch of the beast's high-altitude life for the first day after butchering. Makes for an exceptional base to any Refined or Masterwork preparation.

items.name: Ōkami no Abura 狼の脂 (Mountain God's Rendered Fat)

description.value:
Ōkami no Abura 狼の脂 (Mountain God's Rendered Fat)

Thick layers of pale winter fat from beneath the hide, rendered down over a long fire into a clear, amber-gold tallow. A spoonful transforms any pan-fry — meat sears faster, vegetables crisp cleaner, and the aroma carries a distant suggestion of thunder. Keeps indefinitely if stored cold.

DM Notes

**One-time harvest.** 6 portions total from the Yama-no-Ōkami harvest. Single-grade-locked at 極上 Gokujō — the nat-20 harvest check cleared the Legendary threshold and secured every cut at top grade. Party currently holds the full 6 portions. Track usage in campaign-state.md.
